case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v District Judge, Unnao and Others
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows: ...

The Prescribed Authority constituted under the U. P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act determined the compensation payable to respondents 3 to 6 for acquisition of the surplus land and trees in the amount of Rs. 90, 637.20 p.
Respondents 3 to 6 contested the application seeking condonation of the delay.
The learned District Judge held that the order under appeal was dated January 25, 1972 and the appeal was filed on September 19, 1972 and that prima facie it was barred by limitation.
The present appellant approached the High Court in Writ Petition No. 610 of 1974 u/art. 227 of the Constitution.
Art. 227 or Art. 226 were devised to advance justice and not to thwart it.
issues: Whether the appeal was barred by limitation
Whether the delay in preferring the appeal should be condoned
petitioner_arguments: The appellant simultaneously filed an application u/s. 5 of the Limitation Act for condoning the delay in preferring the appeal.

The explanation for not filing the appeal in time is not very convincing and that even though the concerned department had the knowledge about the order which was to be questioned in appeal, right from January 25, 1972, the appellant failed to explain each days delay
Accepting the finding of the High Court that sitting as trial court, it was satisfied that the appellant had made out sufficient cause for condoning the delay
respondent_arguments: The respondents contested the application seeking condonation of the delay.
The allegation that Lekhpal and Sadar kanungo were in collusion with the answering respondents does not carry conviction.
court_reasoning: The learned District Judge noted the fact that the order under appeal was dated January 25, 1972 and the appeal was filed on September 19, 1972 and that prima facie it was barred by limitation.

The learned District Judge further held that the explanation for not filing the appeal in time is not very convincing and that even though the concerned department had the knowledge about the order which was to be questioned in appeal, right from January 25, 1972, the appellant failed to explain each days delay
Approaching the matter from this angle, the learned District Judge rejected the application praying for condonation of delay and dismissed the appeal as barred by limitation.
This is frankly ununderstandable and exhibits a rigid and inflexible view of jurisdiction u/art. 227 ultimately leading to injustice.
Art. 227 or Art. 226 were devised to advance justice and not to thwart it.
holding: The application made u/s. 5 of the Limitation Act by the present appellant seeking condonation of delay in preferring the appeal before the learned District Magistrate is granted and delay is condoned and the appeal is admitted to file.
This appeal is allowed and the Order and Judgment of the leaned District Judge as well as of the High Court are set aside.
The matter is remitted to learned District Judge with a direction to dispose of the appeal on merits.
